title: Are Domain Generalization Benchmarks with Accuracy on the Line Misspecified?

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the correlation between in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) accuracy ('accuracy on the line') across various domain generalization benchmarks to detect model reliance on unstable statistical shortcuts (e.g., image backgrounds, hospital origins, or color annotations).
Measuring ID vs. OOD accuracy correlations for toxicity classification on the CivilComments dataset across subpopulation data splits mentioning male or female identities.
Measuring ID vs. OOD accuracy correlations for toxicity classification on the CivilComments dataset across subpopulation data splits mentioning Black or White identities.
Measuring ID vs. OOD accuracy correlations for toxicity classification on the CivilComments dataset across subpopulation data splits mentioning Christian, Muslim, or other religious identities.
Measuring ID vs. OOD accuracy correlations for toxicity classification on the CivilComments dataset across subpopulation data splits mentioning LGBTQ identities.
